Alien Animals

Alien Animals: Roll once on the following table to determine the animal type that is encountered. This roll is modified by the Terrain DM.

*Alternating Trait Generation DM: Alternate rolling the positive and negative DM every trait roll.

pages.name: Alien Animal Creation
pages.html:
Alien Animal Creation

Alien Animal Creation: Roll 2D on the Animal Creation Table to generate a unique alien creature, applying any applicable terrain DM to the Size column. The following is a description of each animal variable:

  • Size: The size of the animal determines the difficulty it takes to attack them. Tiny animals in a swarm (6 or more together) are considered Average (8+) difficulty to hit.
  • Hits: This indicates the amount of damage an animal can take before being killed. As a rule of thumb, animals can take 1/2 the number of hits before being pinned and 3/4 the number of hits before becoming unconscious.
  • Damage: This is the amount of damage a single animal of this type is capable of inflicting when they attack.
  • Behaviour: Roll 1D and determine the behavioural type of this animal. This will be used for determining behaviour on the Characteristic Table below.
  • Number of traits: Each animal will have a trait, with larger animals having more. Use this column to determine how many an animal has.
  • Number appearing: This represents the number appearing when encountered. All animals are considered identical in terms of behavior, traits, hits, and damage.
  • Earth examples: This column is to help visualize the size of an animal based on the real world.

pages.name: Alien Animal Characteristic Descriptions
pages.html:
Alien Animal Characteristic Descriptions

Alien Animal Characteristic descriptions: The following are the descriptions of the different type of alien animals found on the prior table.

  • Carrion-Eater: This animal primarily consumes dead animal flesh, usually after other animals have finished feeding.
  • Chaser: This animal will pursue prey, usually in packs.
  • Eater: This animal will eat anything edible, an omnivore without preference.
  • Filter: This animal feeds by allowing the environment to pass through it’s filter to capture food. Usually applied to slow moving animals that are in water or the air.
  • Gatherer: This animal will collect food it finds and consume it along with storing and sharing with other similar animals.
  • Grazer: This animal spends most of its time grazing on plant-matter and may be found in herds or alone.
  • Hunter: This animal will patiently stalk prey until it's the ideal time to strike. Hunters usually aren't as strong at chasing so they will oftentimes work in a group and possibly with tools to help acquire food. Hunters may be omnivore but will lean towards carnivore if given the opportunity.
  • Intermittent: This animal will spend time between grazing and gathering plant matter for food, often alone.
  • Intimidator: This animal will attempt to steal food from others violently, oftentimes with a pack as well. They focus on aggression to scare other animals away from their food.
  • Killer: This animal is a predator that isn't hesitant to hunt an animal, regardless of the prey’s size. This animal is driven to fight for its food without apprehension.
  • Pouncer: This animal is an ambush hunter, who focuses on waiting for prey to pass by. Pouncers usually are hunters, but focus on taking their prey by surprise rather than out-witting them. Pouncers are solitary.
  • Reducer: This animal will consume all remaining biological matter from a food source once it has been picked apart by other, larger animals. Reducers usually are applied to swarms of tiny animals that breakdown the matter for sustenance.
  • Robber: This animal focuses on stealing hunted or captured food from other animals but when it is opportune and wouldn't result in potential harm to themselves. Usually these animals are large and/or aggressive to allow them to succeed.
  • Siren: This animal will attract prey using sound, smell, color, patterns, etc. to then trap them. Sirens may also use the same lure to alert other animals in their pack about danger.
  • Trapper: This animal constructs a trap and awaits for potential prey to fall into it or become ensnared in some capacity to prevent the prey from fleeing.

Book p.112

Alien Animal Traits

Alien Animal Traits: The following are different animal traits based on the animal’s behaviour.

  • Determine Alien Animal Trait: Roll 1D+ terrain DM to the associated animal behaviour. Roll a number of times as determined by the Number of Traits column on the Alien Animal Generation Table.
  • Remember: These are just traits to help it survive its environment, but it is assumed the animal is built for its environment. For example, if in an ocean environment, it is assumed the animal swims and lives under the water.

pages.name: Animal Trait Descriptions
pages.html:
Animal Trait Description

  • Alarm: The animal will release a sound, scent, or visual behavior to attract 2D more of the same type to protect the frightened animal.
  • Amphibious: The animal can live both in liquid and on land for long durations of time.
  • Armour: This animal has armour equal to 1D.
  • Bioelectric: This animal can protect itself with a natural electricity attack that is as powerful as a stun weapon.
  • Camouflaged: The animal blends into its native environment well, granting it Stealth 2, and it gains a +2 DM to contested checks to spot the animal.
  • Dark Sight: This animal can see in the ultraviolet or infrared spectrums or other spectrums that humans cannot see in.
  • Diseased: This animal’s successful attack deals an ongoing 1D damage every hour until the target makes a 8+ END save. See Disease for more information.
  • Echolocation: Allows the creature to see via sound. May be a secondary form of sight, such as when in the dark.
  • Fast: This animal is quick, and is able to move or attack a second time each combat round.
  • Flyer: The animal can float and/or fly by using wings, inflatable air sacks, membranes, and other means of navigating the sky.
  • Heightened senses: This animal has +1 DM to any roll that helps it survive, including attacking or seeking food.
  • Incandescent: This animal is capable of creating light when in a dark location.
  • Pheromone: This animal is able to engage in more complex communication with other similar animals by releasing pheromones in the air, based on their emotional state.
  • Poison: This animal causes 1D continuous damage to its target every round until a successful average (8+) END roll or the target is treated with first aid. See Poison for more information.
  • Psionic: This animal is psionically attuned and can detect the minds of nearby predators or prey. Roll 1D plus any +DM for terrain to determine their PSI score and level in their PSI talent. Psionic animals can use Shield, and any predators have Awareness, while other animals have Teleport.
  • Slow: This animal is slow, and may only move or attack once a combat round.

Book p.113
